germany.name: Germany
germany.tests: IELTS or TOEFL for English-taught programs; TestDaF or DSH for German-taught programs

work.rule: 120 full days or 240 half days per year

germany.visa_notes: National student visa. Proof of funds (blocked account) is usually required.
tips: Many public universities charge only a small semester fee.
Student dorms are cheaper but have waiting lists; apply early.
A semester ticket usually covers local public transport.

canada.name: Canada
canada.tests: IELTS or TOEFL (some universities also accept other tests)

work.rule: Up to 24 hours per week off-campus during study terms

canada.visa_notes: Study permit. A letter of acceptance and proof of funds are required.
tips: Big-city rent is high; smaller cities can save thousands per year.
Check if your province requires an attestation letter.
Co-op programs can pay while you study.

uk.name: United Kingdom
uk.tests: IELTS (UKVI approved test for most visas)

work.rule: Up to 20 hours per week in term time at degree level

uk.visa_notes: Student visa. A confirmation of acceptance for studies (CAS) and proof of funds are required.
tips: London costs far more than other cities.
The Immigration Health Surcharge is paid with the visa application.
Most master degrees take one year, which lowers total cost.

australia.name: Australia

work.rule: Up to 48 hours per fortnight during study periods

australia.visa_notes: Student visa (subclass 500). Overseas Student Health Cover and a Genuine Student statement are required.
tips: Sydney and Melbourne cost more than other cities.
Student visa fees have risen in recent years; check the current amount.
Part-time work rules are generous for students.

usa.name: United States
usa.tests: TOEFL or IELTS; GRE or GMAT for some programs

work.rule: On-campus work up to 20 hours per week; off-campus work is restricted

usa.visa_notes: F-1 student visa. A Form I-20 and proof of funds are required, plus the SEVIS fee.
tips: Health insurance is mandatory and often billed by the university.
Public universities in smaller towns cost much less to live in.
Assistantships can reduce tuition for graduate students.

netherlands.name: Netherlands
netherlands.tests: IELTS or TOEFL for English-taught programs

work.rule: Up to 16 hours per week, or full-time in June to August

netherlands.visa_notes: Residence permit, usually arranged by the university. Proof of funds is required.
tips: Housing is scarce; start looking as soon as you are admitted.
Most universities arrange the residence permit for you.
A bicycle is the cheapest way to get around.
